components.css: :host{--neo-accent:#bce64a;--neo-accent-text:#1e2718;--neo-surface-solid:#202326;--neo-bg-deep:#0b0d0f;--neo-text:#f0f2ef;--neo-muted:#a2aaa5;--neo-faint:#8a938e;--neo-line:rgba(255,255,255,.065);--neo-shadow-dark:rgba(0,0,0,.62);--neo-shadow-light:rgba(68,73,75,.2);font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif}.ds-btn-primary{height:34px;padding:0 14px;border:0;border-radius:12px;background:var(--neo-accent);color:var(--neo-accent-text);font-weight:600;font-size:12px;cursor:pointer;transition:box-shadow .15s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1),transform .15s}.ds-btn-primary:hover{box-shadow:0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb,var(--neo-accent) 55%,transparent),0 6px 18px color-mix(in srgb,var(--neo-accent) 28%,transparent)}.ds-btn-primary:active{transform:scale(.97)}.ds-btn-primary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--neo-accent);outline-offset:2px}

components.css: :host{--neo-accent:#bce64a;--neo-accent-text:#1e2718;--neo-surface-solid:#202326;--neo-bg-deep:#0b0d0f;--neo-text:#f0f2ef;--neo-muted:#a2aaa5;--neo-faint:#8a938e;--neo-line:rgba(255,255,255,.065);--neo-shadow-dark:rgba(0,0,0,.62);--neo-shadow-light:rgba(68,73,75,.2);font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif}.ds-card{width:220px;padding:16px;border:1px solid var(--neo-line);border-radius:14px;background:var(--neo-surface-solid);color:var(--neo-text);box-shadow:3px 3px 8px var(--neo-shadow-dark),-3px -3px 8px var(--neo-shadow-light);transition:transform .22s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1),box-shadow .22s}.ds-card:hover{transform:translateY(-3px);box-shadow:8px 8px 18px var(--neo-shadow-dark),-6px -6px 16px var(--neo-shadow-light)}.ds-card strong{font:700 15px/1.3 Manrope,sans-serif}.ds-card p{margin:6px 0 0;color:var(--neo-muted);font-size:12.5px}

narrative.overview:
Orbi is a professional's desk where every tool is within reach: chat, images, video, voice, workflows, agents and a terminal laid out on one surface. The desk is soft and tactile — controls feel like they rise out of the surface they sit on — and the user's work is always the brightest thing on it. Ornament stays quiet until something is active; then it is bold: the active tab glows, the message box ring circles and breathes, a running node pulses with its own color.

The language is **Adaptive Soft UI**: the same components, sizes, spacing and interaction hierarchy in every theme, with three lighting worlds that change only tokens (color, shadow, border, font and effects):

- **Orbi Dark — Premium Dark Soft UI.** Deep graphite desk, soft lifted surfaces, faint ambient light, Orbit Lime for action.
- **Orbi Light — Soft Neumorphic UI.** Pale sage desk; controls extruded with paired light and dark shadows, pressed controls inset.
- **Orbi Terminal — Cyberpunk Terminal UI.** Near-black desk, phosphor-green text and thin neon borders, monospace everywhere.

Neumorphism is a material here, not a rule: it never costs contrast or makes a clickable thing look like decoration. Every control keeps a visible border or label in addition to its relief.
keyCharacteristics: One component system, three themes; switching theme never moves anything.
Soft relief at rest, bold light on state (active, focus, running, success).
Orbit Lime is the single action color; node hues label media types only.
Rounded, friendly geometry (8–18px), pills for chips and tags.
Manrope for headings, DM Sans for everything else, monospace only in Terminal and code.

rules.name: The One Action Color Rule
rules.body: Only Orbit Lime (Phosphor Green in Terminal) means "do this". Media hues never fill a primary button.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Colors come from `--neo-*` tokens; a hardcoded gray is a bug because it breaks one of the three themes.

rules.name: The 11/12 Floor Rule
rules.body: No UI text below 11px; no sentence below 12px.

rules.name: The Terminal Voice Rule
rules.body: In Terminal every face becomes the monospace stack; sizes and weights stay the same.

rules.name: The Same Grid Rule
rules.body: Every Creative tab uses the same top bar height, column widths and section rhythm, so switching tabs never shifts the frame.

rules.name: The Light-On-State Rule
rules.body: At rest things are soft; when active, focused or running they glow in their color. Never glow something that is idle (the composer's breathing ring is the one invitation).

dos: **Do** build every new screen from the `--neo-*` tokens so it works in Dark, Light and Terminal at once.
**Do** make active, selected and running states bold: lime (or the media hue) plus the active glow.
**Do** keep text at 11px minimum and sentences at 12px; check contrast in all three themes.
**Do** keep the Draft Creative / Daniel Rodrigues signature where the brand requires it (About, exports).
donts: **Don't** hardcode grays or hex text colors in components.
**Don't** use a colored side stripe thicker than 1px, an icon tile above a heading, or gradient text.
**Don't** let neumorphic relief be the only sign that something is clickable.
**Don't** change layout, sizes or positions between themes — only tokens change.
